title: Exactness for the normalized shifts on a native fixed-factor tensor model
statement: Let $C$ be a category with objects in universe $u+1$, morphisms in universe $u$, and $C$ essentially small in universe $u+1$. Let $J$ be a Grothendieck topology on $C$ and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings in universe $u+1$. Use the standard unbounded derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $a$ be a ProjectionRestriction.TensorModel: its bifunctor $T:D(R)\times D(R)\to D(R)$ is naturally identified with signed total tensor on flat-term K-flat pairs, and precomposition with the pair of resolving inclusions is bijective on natural transformations. Let $s$ be TensorShifts for $a$, meaning coherent integer bifunctor shifts whose two representative equations are precisely the signed total-complex equations [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-restriction]. For every $E\in D(R)$, the functor $T(E,-)$, with the second-variable shift supplied by $s$, is triangulated. No bound on E or on the varying input is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor; Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; more-algebra.tex, Tag 0FNH, item-shift-tensor.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution P of a complex representing E. Convert the termwise tensor-right exactness to IsFlatOnSite through siteSheafTensorRightIso. The fixed K-flat tensor theorem supplies a coherent shift structure on the published derived tensor, exactness at Q(P), and a shift-compatible computation isomorphism c whose resolving components are representativeIso.

Apply the proved normalized tensor model isomorphism to a. It gives a natural bifunctor isomorphism e from the published tensor to a.functor, with representativeIso followed by e exactly equal to a.representative on every resolving pair.

The second normalization field of TensorShifts makes the fixed-factor representative comparison commute with every integer shift: postcompose its equation by the shifted forward representative and cancel the inverse. Shift stability of resolving complexes follows from the same field. Restrict c to resolving varying arguments. The restriction of the fixed-factor part of e equals the inverse of this restriction followed by the specified representative comparison, so it commutes with shifts. Resolving localization is essentially surjective, by the flat resolution above, and the shift-compatibility reflection lemma NatTrans.CommShift.of_whiskerLeft therefore proves that the fixed-factor part of e commutes with shifts on all derived objects. Functor.isTriangulated_of_iso transfers exactness at Q(P). Finally the resolving isomorphism Q(P) to E induces a shift-compatible isomorphism by sa.shifts.commShift_map, and the same lemma transfers exactness to E. These are proved categorical calculations in the item module; no pullback, slice comparison, or bound is used.

proof_origin.place: Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor and preceding exact localization construction), Tag 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution); more-algebra.tex Tag 0FNH (item-shift-tensor). The normalized comparison and shift reflection are proved explicitly from the existing cochain rigidity and fixed K-flat exactness statements.
